quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The library closes at nine tonight
quests.punctuatedSentence: The library closes at nine tonight.
quests.ruleExplanation: A sentence that states a fact ends with a period, the most neutral end mark.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence is simply reporting information, not asking or exclaiming anything.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The library closes at nine tonight ➔ Final: The library closes at nine tonight.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: My uncle repairs bicycles on weekends
quests.punctuatedSentence: My uncle repairs bicycles on weekends.
quests.ruleExplanation: Statements that simply describe something keep a level tone and close with a period.
quests.nativeTip: Read the sentence aloud - does your voice rise at the end, or stay level?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: My uncle repairs bicycles on weekends ➔ Final: My uncle repairs bicycles on weekends.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Please close the window before you leave
quests.punctuatedSentence: Please close the window before you leave.
quests.ruleExplanation: A polite request is a statement in form, so it ends with a period.
quests.nativeTip: Even a polite request is still delivered in a calm, matter-of-fact way.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Please close the window before you leave ➔ Final: Please close the window before you leave.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Have you finished your homework yet
quests.punctuatedSentence: Have you finished your homework yet?
quests.ruleExplanation: A direct question ends with a question mark, no matter how it begins.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence is trying to get information from someone, not give it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Have you finished your homework yet ➔ Final: Have you finished your homework yet?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Where did you put the car keys
quests.punctuatedSentence: Where did you put the car keys?
quests.ruleExplanation: Question words like 'where' signal that the sentence is asking, so it needs a question mark.
quests.nativeTip: Questions that start with a word like 'where' or 'why' still need the same closing mark.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Where did you put the car keys ➔ Final: Where did you put the car keys?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Are we still meeting at noon
quests.punctuatedSentence: Are we still meeting at noon?
quests.ruleExplanation: When the verb comes before the subject, as in 'Are we,' the sentence is asking something and needs a question mark.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the sentence starts by flipping the verb before the subject - that's a question pattern.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Are we still meeting at noon ➔ Final: Are we still meeting at noon?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Watch out for that step
quests.punctuatedSentence: Watch out for that step!
quests.ruleExplanation: A warning said with urgency ends with an exclamation mark to show strong feeling.
quests.nativeTip: This isn't calm information - someone needs to react right now.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Watch out for that step ➔ Final: Watch out for that step!

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: We won the championship
quests.punctuatedSentence: We won the championship!
quests.ruleExplanation: Strong excitement or celebration is shown with an exclamation mark instead of a period.
quests.nativeTip: Imagine shouting this news to a friend - how would it sound?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: We won the championship ➔ Final: We won the championship!

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: That was the loudest thunder Ive ever heard
quests.punctuatedSentence: That was the loudest thunder I've ever heard!
quests.ruleExplanation: A sentence expressing surprise or intense feeling takes an exclamation mark, and 'I've' needs its apostrophe for 'I have.'
quests.nativeTip: Surprise and intensity usually don't end quietly, and a contraction is hiding in there too.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: That was the loudest thunder Ive ever heard ➔ Final: That was the loudest thunder I've ever heard!

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (?)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Did the package arrive today
quests.punctuatedSentence: Did the package arrive today?
quests.ruleExplanation: This sentence asks for information, so it needs a question mark, not a period.
quests.nativeTip: First decide: is this sentence asking, telling, or reacting?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Did the package arrive today ➔ Final: Did the package arrive today?

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (.)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The train leaves from platform two
quests.punctuatedSentence: The train leaves from platform two.
quests.ruleExplanation: Because it only states information calmly, it takes a period rather than a question mark or exclamation point.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence simply reports a fact, without asking or reacting.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The train leaves from platform two ➔ Final: The train leaves from platform two.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (!)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I cant believe we actually made it in time
quests.punctuatedSentence: I can't believe we actually made it in time!
quests.ruleExplanation: Phrases showing disbelief or excitement, like 'can't believe,' usually call for an exclamation mark.
quests.nativeTip: The phrase 'can't believe' hints at strong emotion, not a plain fact.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I cant believe we actually made it in time ➔ Final: I can't believe we actually made it in time!

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The basket had apples oranges and bananas
quests.punctuatedSentence: The basket had apples, oranges, and bananas.
quests.ruleExplanation: When three or more items are listed together, a comma follows each item except the last.
quests.nativeTip: Three separate fruits are named in a row - give each one its own space.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The basket had apples oranges and bananas ➔ Final: The basket had apples, oranges, and bananas.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: She packed a towel sunscreen and a hat for the beach
quests.punctuatedSentence: She packed a towel, sunscreen, and a hat for the beach.
quests.ruleExplanation: Each item in a series of three or more gets separated by a comma so the list reads clearly.
quests.nativeTip: Count how many separate things she packed before deciding where the commas go.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: She packed a towel sunscreen and a hat for the beach ➔ Final: She packed a towel, sunscreen, and a hat for the beach.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: We need milk eggs bread and butter from the store
quests.punctuatedSentence: We need milk, eggs, bread, and butter from the store.
quests.ruleExplanation: No matter how many items appear in a list, each one is separated by a comma, including before 'and.'
quests.nativeTip: This list has four items instead of three - the comma pattern still works the same way.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: We need milk eggs bread and butter from the store ➔ Final: We need milk, eggs, bread, and butter from the store.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I dont want to miss the bus
quests.punctuatedSentence: I don't want to miss the bus.
quests.ruleExplanation: The apostrophe in 'don't' stands in for the missing 'o' from 'do not.'
quests.nativeTip: Two words have been joined into one, and a letter is missing from the middle.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I dont want to miss the bus ➔ Final: I don't want to miss the bus.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Shes bringing dessert to the party
quests.punctuatedSentence: She's bringing dessert to the party.
quests.ruleExplanation: An apostrophe replaces the dropped letter when 'she is' becomes 'she's.'
quests.nativeTip: 'She is' has been shortened - where would the missing letter have been?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Shes bringing dessert to the party ➔ Final: She's bringing dessert to the party.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Theyre coming over after dinner
quests.punctuatedSentence: They're coming over after dinner.
quests.ruleExplanation: The apostrophe marks where the 'a' was removed in joining 'they' and 'are.'
quests.nativeTip: Say the full version, 'they are,' and notice which letter disappears when it's shortened.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Theyre coming over after dinner ➔ Final: They're coming over after dinner.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Wont you join us for dinner
quests.punctuatedSentence: Won't you join us for dinner?
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence invites a response, so it needs both the contraction 'won't' and a question mark.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence has two jobs: shorten 'will not' and decide if it's asking or telling.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Wont you join us for dinner ➔ Final: Won't you join us for dinner?

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Its finally stopped raining
quests.punctuatedSentence: It's finally stopped raining!
quests.ruleExplanation: 'It's' is the contraction for 'it is,' and the relief in the sentence calls for an exclamation mark.
quests.nativeTip: Check two things here - does 'it is' need an apostrophe, and does the relief need an exclamation mark?
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Its finally stopped raining ➔ Final: It's finally stopped raining!

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I cant find my phone anywhere
quests.punctuatedSentence: I can't find my phone anywhere.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can't' needs an apostrophe for the missing letters, and since the sentence only states a problem, a period is enough.
quests.nativeTip: This is a plain statement of frustration, not a question or a shout - just add the missing apostrophe.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I cant find my phone anywhere ➔ Final: I can't find my phone anywhere.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: You can choose pizza pasta or salad for lunch
quests.punctuatedSentence: You can choose pizza, pasta, or salad for lunch.
quests.ruleExplanation: A list joined by 'or' follows the same comma pattern as a list joined by 'and.'
quests.nativeTip: This list offers choices instead of naming things someone already has - the comma rule still applies.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: You can choose pizza pasta or salad for lunch ➔ Final: You can choose pizza, pasta, or salad for lunch.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: The coach asked us to run stretch and drink water
quests.punctuatedSentence: The coach asked us to run, stretch, and drink water.
quests.ruleExplanation: A series of actions is punctuated the same way as a series of objects, with commas between each item.
quests.nativeTip: These are three actions in a row, not three objects - the list rule works the same for verbs.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: The coach asked us to run stretch and drink water ➔ Final: The coach asked us to run, stretch, and drink water.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Bring your ID your ticket and your boarding pass
quests.punctuatedSentence: Bring your ID, your ticket, and your boarding pass.
quests.ruleExplanation: Even when list items share a repeated word, each one still needs to be separated by a comma.
quests.nativeTip: Notice each item starts with 'your' - that doesn't change how the commas are placed.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Bring your ID your ticket and your boarding pass ➔ Final: Bring your ID, your ticket, and your boarding pass.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Dont forget your gloves scarf and hat
quests.punctuatedSentence: Don't forget your gloves, scarf, and hat.
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence needs an apostrophe in 'don't' and commas between each item in the list.
quests.nativeTip: Two skills are needed here - fix the shortened word, then separate the three items.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Dont forget your gloves scarf and hat ➔ Final: Don't forget your gloves, scarf, and hat.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Shes bought bread cheese and jam for the picnic
quests.punctuatedSentence: She's bought bread, cheese, and jam for the picnic.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'She's' needs an apostrophe for 'she has,' and the three picnic items need list commas.
quests.nativeTip: Look for both a missing apostrophe and a list that needs commas.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Shes bought bread cheese and jam for the picnic ➔ Final: She's bought bread, cheese, and jam for the picnic.

quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Theyre selling shirts hats and bags at the fair
quests.punctuatedSentence: They're selling shirts, hats, and bags at the fair.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'They're' stands for 'they are,' and each item in the list of goods needs its own comma.
quests.nativeTip: Check the contraction first, then count how many items are being sold.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Theyre selling shirts hats and bags at the fair ➔ Final: They're selling shirts, hats, and bags at the fair.

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (?)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Could you grab milk bread and eggs on your way home
quests.punctuatedSentence: Could you grab milk, bread, and eggs on your way home?
quests.ruleExplanation: The sentence asks something, so it ends with a question mark, and its three items are separated by commas.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence is a request phrased as a question, and it also lists several items.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Could you grab milk bread and eggs on your way home ➔ Final: Could you grab milk, bread, and eggs on your way home?

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (!)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: I cant believe how fast this year went
quests.punctuatedSentence: I can't believe how fast this year went!
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Can't' requires an apostrophe, and the disbelief expressed calls for an exclamation mark rather than a period.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs a missing apostrophe, and its tone suggests more than a calm statement.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: I cant believe how fast this year went ➔ Final: I can't believe how fast this year went!

quests.conceptTitle: Punctuation Conductor: Sentence Purpose & End Punctuation (?)
quests.unpunctuatedSentence: Werent you supposed to call me this morning
quests.punctuatedSentence: Weren't you supposed to call me this morning?
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Weren't' takes an apostrophe for the missing letters, and since the sentence questions someone, it ends with a question mark.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence needs a contraction fixed and is clearly asking something.
quests.visualAnchor: 🖋️ Raw: Werent you supposed to call me this morning ➔ Final: Weren't you supposed to call me this morning?
